one_star_reviews.text:
If I could give Riseholme College zero stars, I genuinely would. My experience there has been one of the biggest disappointments I’ve had, and I honestly feel like the college has wasted an entire year of my life.

I went into Riseholme wanting to actually achieve something and work towards what I wanted to do, but instead I spent a huge amount of my time dealing with problems that made both college and my personal life unnecessarily difficult. I feel like I didn’t get anywhere near the outcome I should have achieved because of the situation I was put in.

The way bullying was handled was particularly disgusting from my perspective. It genuinely felt like the college was more willing to accommodate and reward the person causing the problems than properly support the person on the receiving end. When someone can make another student’s life extremely difficult and still appear to receive praise, rewards and favourable treatment, it sends a pretty awful message about what the college actually tolerates.

The lessons were honestly shit. The teaching and support were nowhere near what I expected, and there were times when it felt like teachers simply couldn’t be bothered to properly help. You’re left wondering what exactly you’re paying for when the people who are supposed to support you don’t seem interested in actually listening or helping you succeed.

Another massive issue was how I felt students without special educational needs were treated. I completely understand that students with additional needs deserve support — obviously they do. But supporting one group of students should never mean completely neglecting another. From my experience, it felt like students without additional needs were pushed to the side, expected to just get on with everything themselves and treated as though their problems didn’t matter.

What makes it worse is that this wasn’t just a bad few weeks. This affected my entire college experience and ultimately interfered with what I wanted to achieve. I came to college with plans and ambitions, and I am leaving feeling like a year that I could have spent progressing towards my future has been thrown away.

Riseholme seriously needs to look at how it handles bullying, how it supports students and whether it actually listens to the students who are struggling. Because from where I was standing, it felt like the people who needed to be heard weren’t being heard at all.

I wouldn’t recommend Riseholme College based on my experience. If you’re considering going here, I’d seriously think twice and make sure you properly research what the student support is actually like before committing to it.

A year wasted, a lot of unnecessary stress, and an experience I absolutely wouldn’t repeat.

one_star_reviews.text: Absolutely the worst they purposely mess around with your script with no oversight

If this trip resembled meat, it would be dry, saltless, week-old gammon! Terrible.

The journey down was great with a splendid driver who stopped when asked and was cheerful, but the journey back had as much joy as driving the wrong way down the A19 with two working tires.

We had arranged and paid to be picked up and brought back to our initial pickup point. However, we were then informed on the day that they would send a large coach to pick up us plus two other groups, dropping them off before us at various locations, extending the journey by some time. To make matters worse, we were told we had to push our pickup time back because one of the groups didn't want to leave early. Sorry, but didn't we pay for our group and our chosen time?

As for the journey, we were told there would be complimentary water, which then wasn't provided. This would have been fine if the bus had ventilation and wasn't hot enough to cook a Greggs steak bake! We were also informed there would be charging ports aboard, of which there were none. This led me to spend the journey sweating and staring at the back of the seat in front of me whilst the driver flew up the country roads as if he were a prime Michael Schumacher.

As for the process of contacting the company, we were made aware that we had too much luggage going back after confirming what we had prior to the trip. We were away for 4 days so had to take suitable amounts of luggage, as we aren't exactly going to take part in Netflix's 4th season of "Outlast" and just take the clothes on our backs?

Overall, a terrible experience, bar the journey down which was splendid.

So yes, gammon. Dry, tasteless, cold gammon. Avoid at all costs.

(Big up Steve, though, our driver on the way there)

Extremely disappointing experience from start to finish.

We ordered a king-size mattress on 9 July and were assured by the sales assistant in-store that it would be delivered on 5 August. Although this was already quite a long lead time, we accepted it based on that promise.

As the delivery date approached, we received no communication whatsoever regarding a delivery slot. After spending two hours trying to get through to customer service, we finally discovered that the store had never actually placed our order. We were then told that the new delivery date would be 27 August, more than seven weeks after the original purchase date.

To make matters worse, following this conversation we received a confirmation showing a double mattress scheduled for delivery on 27 August, despite the fact that we had ordered a king-size mattress. We immediately queried this by email but never received a response.

The entire experience has been incredibly frustrating. Customer service appears to be overwhelmed, with minimum waiting times of around two hours on chat, and the overall service felt disorganised, sloppy, and poorly managed.

We were particularly disappointed because we have guests staying with us and specifically needed the mattress well before the end of summer. Given the repeated mistakes, lack of communication, and poor customer support, we ultimately cancelled the order and will not be shopping with Dreams again.

I would not recommend Dreams based on this experience.

Edit:
The customer service promised the refund will be with us within 7-10 working days. We are now pushing 13 working days and wondering whether DREAMS stole money from us and never intends to refund it.

one_star_reviews.text:
My biggest issue with this place has been how my mental health has been handled alongside my alcohol withdrawal.
I have a diagnosed anxiety disorder, and during my stay I repeatedly explained that Librium helps control my physical alcohol-withdrawal symptoms, but it does not adequately control my underlying mental-health anxiety. Despite explaining this, I felt that some nursing staff treated the fact that Librium is a benzodiazepine as though that automatically meant my anxiety was being adequately treated.

For me, those are two different issues. My withdrawal symptoms and my underlying anxiety are not the same thing, and I felt that my mental-health symptoms were prolonged because they weren't being properly listened to or understood.
What made this particularly frustrating was the inconsistency between nurses. Some staff seemed to understand my situation and were supportive, while others took a completely different approach to my prescribed medication. When you're already in aan unfamiliar environment, going through withdrawal and dealing with severe anxiety, that inconsistency can make an already difficult situation considerably worse. Staff can be very rude and horrible tone

There have been some caring members of staff and a lot of hca dont smile or look like they want to be here overall I feel that my mental health should have been taken more seriously as a separate issue from my withdrawal. I came here to get better, and instead there were times when I felt that the way my anxiety was handled made an already difficult experience even harder.
however my consultant has been very good just whole thing let down by incompetent nurses

Ran out my pain meds gave me significantly less while waiting to order some in just terrible.

Update i self discharged as I was off detox and was fine but they didn't warn me about possible clonazepam withdrawal and gave me none to take home I ended up in a&e in seriouse condition due to no meds now been prescribed by nhs. They have made claims they warned me about this which is false they said i should stay for further addiction/mental health therapy.

one_star_reviews.text:
The environment was painful for me due to autistic hypersensitivity. I asked for it to be modified to be less painful which is my right under the Equality Act as the Equality Act says if a disabled person has a disadvantage in an environment, the organisation is legally obliged to modify it to make their experience closer to that of a non-disabled person, even if it means making exceptions to their usual policy. It's called Reasonable Adjustments.

At 1st this was done and it helped, but then they suddenly said they couldn't do anymore as it was "against policy". I tried to point out the entire point of Reasonable Adjustments is organisations are obliged to provide them even if it means changing policy, otherwise they could justify any inequity against disabled people with "it's just our policy". They're only allowed to refuse if there's an external reason why it wouldn't work like "it wouldn't actually help your disability" or "it would be asking a huge, unprecedented level of resources from us" so I asked them to give this but they ignored me and repeated "it's our policy". In the end they insisted on numbing me with high dose benzos instead of just creating a suitable environment for me in the 1st place.

When I complained they said "we had to act in accordance with The Priory procedures" but that's not a justification, it's what I complained about in the 1st place. I said "the issue is "we won't change the environment to help your disability because this environment is just our policy" is a violation of your legal duties to disabled people" and they said "we did it that way because it's our policy". Stellar job. There aren't words to describe how circular this reasoning is. They didn't even attempt to say "this isn't how the Equality Act works" (if they did it wouldn't be correct but at least it would be responding to my actual point)

The worst part is they said "I understand you're autistic and changes to your environment can be distressing" as it misses the point. Struggling to accept change is a real autistic trait, but it's not the relevant trait here. The problem is my brain physically doesn't know how to process sensory info normally and registers certain "normal" input as painful because it has more connections than normal (look up synaptic pruning in autistic vs non-autistic people) so whenever there's sensory input more paths "light up" than normal, so the brain has a lower threshold for how much info is "too much" and the path between the sensory centre and the pain centre lights up more easily.

The response implies the environment would be fine for me if it was my routine and that I could just get used to it and it would be fine, but that's not true. Repeated exposure to overstimulating environments actually makes my tolerance lower as the energy I need to cope is used faster than it's restored, which leads to something called burnout, where I'm so exhausted that it lowers my pain threshold even more. The only way to avoid the distress is to avoid being in an overstimulating environment in the first place, hence my request for adjustment.

The staff's behaviour at the time and the complaint response both suggest they thought I was just throwing a tiff because I didn’t like my routine environment being changed and they didn't understand (or didn't care) that I was in actual physical pain, and this is incredibly hurtful.

Another issue is the care team said to continue treatment after discharge and discussed whether to stay with them with my insurance or switch to NHS and decided to continue with the same therapist from their team. Only when I left hospital did I find out he wasn't covered by my insurance, so my treatment didn't continue as promised. In the complaint response they said "it's not the inpatient team's fault your therapist wasn't covered by your insurance" which again misses the point because what WAS in their control was the planning and they should have checked the therapist they planned to put me with would be covered by the insurance they knew I was on.

Just a waste in the end.
The Oak ward treating me like an animal call 999 they will help you if you being treated like an animal

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Mercedes-Benz Milton Keynes has been one of the most stressful customer service experiences I have ever had.

My car has been in their possession since 7/07/2026, two months, yet I have received very little communication or reassurance. I have had to chase for updates instead of being kept informed. I was told that parts were expected by the end of September, but since then I have heard nothing to confirm whether they have even arrived and today is 6/10/26.

I own a seven-seater, yet I was provided with a five-seater courtesy car without anyone discussing it with me or asking whether it met my family's needs. On top of that, I have had to deal with the increased insurance costs associated with the loan vehicle.

What has disappointed me most is the complete lack of customer care. No one has contacted me to ask how I am coping without my vehicle, to explain the delays properly, or to give me confidence that my case is being taken seriously.

I am also extremely concerned because documents appear to have been signed in my name without my knowledge or consent. This is now part of my formal complaint and is one of the most serious aspects of this whole experience.

Mercedes-Benz is a premium brand, and customers rightly expect premium service. Unfortunately, my experience at the Milton Keynes dealership has been the exact opposite. After two months of uncertainty, poor communication, and feeling ignored, I have lost confidence in this dealership.

If you're considering using Mercedes-Benz Milton Keynes, I would encourage you to ask detailed questions about communication, courtesy cars, and how customer complaints are handled before trusting them with your vehicle.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐️ 1 STAR — PLEASE READ BEFORE BOOKING

We booked this company to film our wedding because we wanted to preserve the memories of one of the most important days of our lives. Unfortunately, what we received fell so far below what was promised that we feel other couples deserve to know exactly what happened.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that these aren’t simply things we wish had been included. Our booking form specifically states that the service provided includes “Full Bridal Party preparation footage,” “Bride and Bridesmaids’ arrival,” “Footage of the wedding party and the special couple,” and our input into the choice of music used in the film.

Yet this is not what we received.

We are a same-sex couple, and despite there being two brides, the opening preparation footage focuses on my wife while there is no footage of me getting ready at all. There is also no meaningful footage of our guests during the preparations. These aren’t moments we can recreate. They’re gone forever.

Our music requests were also not listened to, despite the booking form explicitly stating that we would have input into the music used.

Our bridesmaids and groomsmen walking down the aisle were initially not included either. I had to specifically demand that this footage be added before it was included.

And then there is the quality of the actual film.

The booking form describes the service as being filmed in full HD 16:9 widescreen, with sound recorded using professional TV-quality microphones, and states that the film would be shot and edited by experienced professionals with many years’ experience.

The finished product simply does not reflect that description.

The footage is poorly framed, with shots that are so low and awkwardly positioned that parts of the film genuinely look like they were recorded by an inexperienced amateur. The lighting is inconsistent and poorly handled throughout. The editing is equally disappointing, with childish sparkles, distracting transitions and awkward camera cuts that look completely out of place in what should have been an elegant wedding film.

There is very little sense of thoughtful editing or storytelling. It feels as though footage has been thrown together rather than carefully selected, cut and crafted into a professional wedding film.

And that’s the part that hurts the most.

You only get one wedding day.

You can’t go back and film the bride who wasn’t filmed getting ready. You can’t recreate the guests who weren’t captured. You can’t redo the wedding party walking down the aisle. You can’t recreate those little moments that happened once and only once.

We paid a professional to preserve those memories, and instead we are left with a finished product that does not properly represent our wedding day.

I am not someone who expects absolute perfection, and I understand that wedding videography can never capture every single moment. But when a company specifically promises certain things in writing, you reasonably expect those things to actually be delivered — particularly when you’re paying to capture memories that can never be replaced.

This review isn’t about being unnecessarily harsh. It is about making other couples aware of our experience before they make the same decision.

Please read the promises on the booking form carefully and compare them with what you actually receive.

If your wedding memories are as important to you as ours were to us, I would strongly recommend asking very detailed questions about exactly what will be filmed, who will be represented, what editing will be carried out, and what happens if agreed elements are missing.

We trusted this company with something we can never do again.

We will always have our wedding day.

Unfortunately, we will never have the wedding film we were promised.

Very disappointing experience with Louis Kennedy Solicitors.

I initially contacted the firm regarding dependant visa applications for my wife and daughter and was told £300 per person. When I later contacted them to proceed, I was quoted £1,800, which was eventually reduced to £1,500 after discussion, and I made the payment.

When the applications were about to be submitted, I was then asked for my card details to pay another £648 in Home Office application fees. I immediately raised my concern and explained that I thought the amount I had already paid covered everything, as nobody had made it clear to me beforehand that the Home Office fees would be additional.

Before I made the additional Home Office payment, I raised all of these concerns with Mr Anil. He told me to proceed with the payment and submit the applications, and that I could contact the office afterwards regarding a partial refund. This convinced me to proceed with the additional payment.

When I later contacted the firm and requested the partial refund that had been discussed before I made the Home Office payment, they refused my request.

Another major concern was the advice I received about the applications themselves. My Skilled Worker occupation code is SOC 6135, and I was informed that there were restrictions on dependants under this occupation. However, during my discussions with the solicitor, I was also told that they had a 100% success rate with similar applications and that similar cases they had handled had been successful. This gave me confidence to proceed with the applications despite the restrictions.

Unfortunately, after paying £1,500 in professional fees plus £648 in Home Office fees, both my wife’s and daughter’s dependant visa applications were refused.

I subsequently raised my concerns formally with the firm, but they rejected my complaint and refused my request for a partial refund.

Based on my personal experience, I am extremely disappointed with the communication, transparency around the costs and the overall service I received. I would not use this firm again.

Very disappointing experience – I would avoid this branch

I visited National Tyres and Autocare Leicester (Blackbird Road LE4) around two weeks ago to have two tyres replaced. I paid for brand-new tyres, new valves and wheel balancing.

I was told that the new valves had been fitted. However, I later discovered that the valves had not actually been replaced. Within a few days, both tyres went flat.

I returned to the branch to have the issue checked, but unfortunately they refused to replace the valves and instead told me that the wheel was damaged. This was particularly frustrating because I had specifically paid for new valves when the tyres were fitted.

I also had a very poor experience with the battery diagnosis. I was given a battery diagnosis that I believe was incorrect and was recommended a battery that was not suitable for my car.

I dealt with Niraj and Kieran, and unfortunately I did not find the service or professionalism acceptable. The whole experience left me feeling that I had paid for work that had not been carried out as promised and then had difficulty getting the issue resolved.

For a company offering tyre fitting, balancing and battery testing, I expected much better attention to detail and customer service.

Based on my experience, I would strongly recommend checking the work carefully before leaving this branch and, personally, I would avoid using it again.

This review reflects my personal experience at this branch.

I hate leaving negative reviews but unfortunately, I’ve had more bad experiences at this branch than good. One example: ordered a heated drying rack on click and collect. Travelled on the metro to collect it and then back home only to find out I’d been given a shelf? Returned to Argos the next day. Not even an apology. Fine, mistakes happen.
Second example: bought a very expensive set of headphones. Returned 2 days later as I had tried them at home and realized I wanted the more expensive upgrade. Tried to return it so I could do just that - rudest customer service I’ve ever had. The lady I dealt with looked disgusted that I’d even deigned to consider to return it. Genuinely my mistake, the Argos return policy does not specifically list headphones as a “wearable item”. It was daft of me to think I could put a plastic object on me and try to return it I suppose but good lord, the Argos customer service returns process was terrible. I will not ever shop with Argos again given these experiences.

one_star_reviews.text:
Really disappointing meal at The Sandpiper, Melton (Marston’s).

We waited over an hour for our food, which was even more frustrating because the pub was pretty deserted and certainly didn’t appear busy.

When the food finally arrived, the nacho cheese bites were literally hollow. Not just a little short on filling — there was practically no cheese inside them at all. The photo really says it all.

What made it worse was the response when I brought this to the attention of the staff. There was no apology and no real attempt to put it right. I was essentially told that they “can’t control what they serve”, that it would be mentioned to the chef, and that was it. No replacement, no refund offered, nothing.

Mistakes happen, and food can occasionally go wrong, but good customer service is about how those problems are handled. Unfortunately, the response here was just as disappointing as the food.

Based on the very long wait, the poor quality of the food and the way the complaint was dealt with, I wouldn’t recommend The Sandpiper and wouldn’t choose to eat here again.

It was awful to put it bluntly. I work in hospitality (yes I’m going to be that person) and if I was the General Manager of there I’d be embarrassed!
Firstly, 40% offer - not running those offers over a Bank Holiday is old hat - with cost of living and so many other options, there is no place for that anymore . It wasn’t busy, to the effect of one staff member behind the bar with a queue whilst the other two were chatting and then one on her phone ! So maybe had you had the offer in use they’d actually have work to do.
Onto food - we were going to have carvery , but once I had a look at it , lack of vegetable choice and how dry it looked I decided to go with the Indian Feast. When it was brought out to me I thought it was a joke - I’ve just paid £25 for a couple of normal wings with a blob of curry sauce on, 2 lamb kebabs that were pale, a couple of pieces of chicken that had just looked at spice, and then the pakoras - well I’ve never seen pakoras like that . I bit into one and I’ve never had chicken so dry in my life! Awful!
Now i would have complained, but no one bothered to check back on us after we got our food and I’m certainly not walking to the bar to complain with my plate of food .
Our bill came to over £85 for three people with soft drinks which is ridiculous for what we received and even this morning I’m still fuming that I paid that amount of money for less than basic food and zero customer service .
Won’t be recommending and won’t be back.

Very poor workmanship and aftercare
Unfortunately, our experience with this contractor has been extremely disappointing. We have had issues with the patios, driveways and pathways on our new build development.

The patio at our new-build property developed numerous loose slabs and the contractor has subsequently undertaken remedial works on three separate occasions, alongside multiple visits from foremen to inspect the problems. Despite being given repeated opportunities to put the work right, further slabs have continued to become loose and concerns remain regarding the quality of the original installation.

The most recent remedial works were particularly unacceptable. Cutting works generated a significant amount of dust and debris which was left across our patio, garden furniture, windows, bifold doors and external areas of the house. We subsequently had to arrange professional cleaning.

What has been equally disappointing is the response afterwards. Rather than acknowledging the problems and taking responsibility, we received comments containing a number of factual assertions that we strongly dispute. The attitude demonstrated during the most recent visit from a foreman also did nothing to restore our confidence.

After three separate attempts at remedial works and multiple inspections, we have completely lost confidence in this contractor and have informed the developer that we will not permit them to undertake any further work at our property.

Problems can occur with construction work; what matters is how a contractor responds when they do. In our experience, repeated unsuccessful repairs, the condition our property was left in and the subsequent handling of our concerns have been extremely disappointing.

Based on our experience, we could not recommend this contractor.

The Check-In Report also records blinds that were detached, not working or had loose fittings, yet these have still not been repaired.

The 193-page independent Check-In Report itself records numerous defects and maintenance issues, yet more than a month after moving in, many of these issues remain unresolved.

After the tenancy started, we were given a contact and told to approach them with any problems. In reality, the experience has involved long waits for email responses and repeated explanations that the property was simply “let as seen”, rather than practical solutions and clear repair dates.

Everything stated here reflects my actual rental experience and the documented condition at check-in.

Very disappointing. Based on my experience, I would recommend prospective tenants consider other agents.

These are only a few examples — there are far too many issues and supporting photographs to list them all individually here.

I fully accept that this is an older property and not newly refurbished. My complaint is not about normal wear and tear. It is about basic functionality, maintenance, cleanliness and hygiene — all of which, in my experience, fell well below a reasonable handover standard.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointing experience despite a good concept

We had a Sublime Science party last week, and while the idea behind it is excellent, the actual delivery was very disappointing.

I don’t like to tarnish small businesses, and I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel I have to be honest about our experience.

The entertainer simply lacked the enthusiasm, energy and even the voice needed for a children’s party. She used a handheld microphone throughout, but it was still difficult to hear her clearly.

She carried out a number of experiments, but there was very little explanation of what she was doing or why it was interesting. The children watched for a short while, but without much interaction or storytelling, most of them quickly lost interest. Within about 30 minutes, the majority of the children were wandering off, chatting among themselves, and running around the room entertaining themselves.

The format also didn’t work well for a larger group. Giving each child an individual turn meant that the other children spent a lot of time waiting, which led to boredom and disengagement.

Considering the package i got which was platinum spent £380, I expected a much more professional and engaging experience.

It’s a real shame because the concept has a lot of potential, but based on our experience I wouldn’t recommend this particular comoany, particularly for larger parties where keeping the children engaged is so important.

I am compelled to share my recent experience, which I believe raises significant red flags that prospective buyers should consider very carefully. My interactions with this agency have been deeply unsatisfactory, & I am not alone in this sentiment the volume of negative reviews should serve as a stark warning to anyone considering doing business here.

I recently placed a bid on a property via auction. I was the sole bidder, & while I accepted the vendor's decision not to proceed with my offer at that time, the situation has since taken a troubling turn. One week later, the same property was relisted, & my previous offer remained as the baseline. Given the lack of competition and the circumstances, I naturally sought to rebid at a revised & reasonable lower figure.

When I contacted the local estate agent, who is listed as the key holder, I was met with resistance. Rather than facilitating a transparent process, I was pressured to submit a higher offer, despite there being no competitive interest in the property. When I questioned this, I was summarily directed to take my concerns up with IAMSOLD.

That is where the situation has become truly unacceptable. For nearly a week, I have made repeated phone calls & sent multiple emails to IAMSOLD, yet I have received absolutely no response. This is a stark contrast to my initial experience, during which I received immediate & persistent attention from their team. Now, having raised a legitimate query, I have been met with complete radio silence.

This level of non-communication & the apparent disregard for a serious buyer is not only unprofessional but deeply concerning. I strongly advise potential buyers to approach with extreme caution & to thoroughly read the existing reviews before engaging with this company. The pattern of behaviour is undeniable, & it should raise everybody's eyebrows.

Absolutely do not recommend. Terrible experience left my daughter upset, anxious and unsafe

I would not recommend this service at all. My daughter went seeking help and came home extremely upset and deeply anxious after her appointment on 25/09/26.

Their stated opening hours are 9am–4pm, yet they offered her slots at 8pm or 6:30pm. She chose 6:30pm as the later time felt too late, and the venue is on Beverley Road which she already didn’t feel comfortable travelling to.

When she arrived, all the shutters were down. She walked all around the building looking for an entrance and phoned the office multiple times — no answer at all. After waiting roughly 15 minutes, the shutters finally opened and her therapist, Adam, came out and simply said: “I’m very sorry, I fell asleep.” Completely unprofessional.

Once inside, his first comment to her was: “Why did you pick a male when you could have picked a female?” My daughter replied that she had simply been told she would be seeing him — she was never given a choice.

To make matters worse, when concerns about travelling were raised, his only reassurance was: “You’ll be okay to get the bus down here.” He booked an out-of-hours appointment, fell asleep leaving a young girl waiting alone outside an unlit building, questioned her choice of therapist, and showed no real care for her safety or wellbeing.

This is not how you treat someone reaching out for support. Avoid at all costs.

I would not recommend joining this gym based on my experience so far. I’ve only been a member for three weeks with my family, and I’m already very disappointed.

The biggest problem is the reception and entry system. The staff often seem under pressure, and there is far too much confusion. We keep being given different information about which facilities my son can use and whether my family needs to sign in separately at reception. One member of staff tells you one thing, then another tells you something completely different.

When you try to explain the problem, instead of feeling listened to, you can end up feeling as though you are the one in the wrong. That is not how paying members should be made to feel.

I don’t necessarily blame the reception staff because they clearly have a lot to deal with. I think the system itself needs to be much better organised, with clear rules that every member of staff understands and follows.

A gym should be somewhere you arrive feeling positive and ready to train, not somewhere you have to worry about what problem you’re going to have at reception that day.

Maybe things will improve in the future, and I genuinely hope they do, but based on my first three weeks, I’m unfortunately not happy with the experience at all.

one_star_reviews.text:
On February 19th I booked and paid for a telehandler course which was due to run on the 13th of April. However when I attended for the first day I found that the course had been cancelled but Citrus has failed to let me know. This caused me to lose a day's holiday and the hassle of rearranging the rest of the week. I rebooked for a course in June and Citrus kept the money I'd already paid. During the course in June, I received an emailed invoice asking me to pay for the course again. I explained to someone in the finance department that I'd already paid and had a paid in full invoice. I thought that was the end of it. I passed the course and was told my card would arrive in 2-3 weeks. After a month of no card I rang Citrus and was told my card was being held for extra quality control checks and it would be sent out soon. However a week later I received another invoice telling me my payment for the course was now overdue. I again rang the finance department and was told I needed to prove I'd paid for the course, and they would not accept their own paid in full invoice that they had sent me. I had to send a screenshot of a bank statement as proof. After another week of no card I called again and was told (mistakenly I believe) that the finance team had OK'd the release of my card. I believe my card was purposely withheld because of their own clerical error of losing track of the money I'd paid in February. I do now have my card today, 2 months after I passed the course. On one positive note, the instructor for the week, I think his name was Lewis Bradbury, was brilliant. Very knowledgeable, patient and supportive, no complaints about him whatsoever.
Will never use Citrus again or recommend them to anyone.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience with UNISON

I have been asking UNISON for meaningful support with a serious employment dispute since December 2025. Over many months I have repeatedly contacted them, supplied extensive documents, completed the forms requested of me and provided further evidence whenever asked.

Despite this, my experience has been one of delay, passing responsibility between people and very little substantive representation.

My case involves a work-related accident, prolonged sickness absence, Occupational Health and return-to-work issues, reasonable-adjustment concerns, clinical supervision, financial consequences and a formal grievance and appeal. These are exactly the circumstances in which I believed trade-union membership would provide meaningful professional support.

Instead, I have repeatedly found myself having to research the issues, organise the evidence, prepare correspondence and progress matters largely on my own.

Most recently, I have been working towards a strict employer grievance-appeal deadline. After repeatedly asking UNISON for help, I was told that I am apparently being “actively represented”. However, the officer identified as providing regional support is unavailable until after my appeal deadline, while I have still been trying to establish what practical help my designated local representative will actually provide.

Saying that a member is “represented” is not the same as actually providing timely advice, reviewing evidence and helping them through an important employment process.

What has been particularly frustrating is that I have not been passive. I have repeatedly chased, supplied documents, produced focused evidence when requested and made clear when deadlines were approaching. After months of this, I should not still be having to ask who is going to help me and what help they are actually going to provide.

I joined a trade union because I expected representation when serious workplace problems arose. My experience has left me questioning what meaningful benefit that membership has provided when I actually needed it.

Based on my experience to date, I would find it very difficult to recommend UNISON to someone who expects prompt, proactive and substantive support during a serious employment dispute.

If UNISON ultimately provides the support it has repeatedly said is available, I will update this review accordingly.

one_star_reviews.text:
I initially contacted this clinic to enquire about fat-dissolving injections and specifically outlined my medical history, as I wanted clear reassurance that the treatment would be safe and appropriate for me before proceeding.

Following my enquiry, I was sent a number of questions via WhatsApp, which I completed in full. An appointment was subsequently arranged through WhatsApp, and I attended the clinic as scheduled. Upon arrival, the reception team could not locate my booking. After further investigation, I was informed that appointments arranged through WhatsApp do not synchronise with the clinic's actual booking system.

This is an astonishingly poor and fundamentally flawed process. From both a customer experience and operational perspective, it is entirely predictable that a disconnected booking system would lead to confusion, missed appointments, wasted journeys, and unnecessary inconvenience for clients.

I was then informed that I would receive a telephone consultation within the hour to discuss the procedure and my medical history. No call was received. Instead, I received a text message at approximately 9:00 pm asking whether I was available to speak. By that time, I was no longer available, and the clinic had already failed to meet the commitment it had made. As a result, I submitted a formal complaint.

The following day, I received a call to discuss the treatment, my concerns, and my medical history. During this conversation, there appeared to be no hesitation or concern regarding my suitability for the procedure. Following that discussion, an appointment was booked for me to attend the clinic, discuss the treatment in more detail, and proceed with the injections.

The evening before the appointment, I received a confirmation message asking whether I was still happy to proceed. I replied confirming that I was and stated that I was looking forward to discussing the procedure in further detail during the appointment.

The very next message I received informed me that the doctor was not comfortable carrying out the procedure.

Frankly, this level of disorganisation and inconsistency is deeply concerning. It demonstrates a complete lack of clinical diligence, poor communication between staff, and an apparent absence of any robust assessment process. It raises serious questions about how treatment decisions are being made and whether appropriate consideration is being given to patient safety before appointments are offered and confirmed.

I responded by asking a very reasonable question: if the doctor was uncomfortable performing the procedure, why did it take more than a week to reach that conclusion? Why was I asked detailed medical questions, reassured during a clinical discussion, offered an appointment, and then invited to proceed, only for the decision to be reversed at the eleventh hour?

The correct and professional approach would have been to advise from the outset that my medical history required further review, that the doctor would conduct additional research or seek further guidance, and that a decision would be communicated once that assessment had been completed. Instead, the clinic led me to believe that the treatment would go ahead, only to withdraw at the last possible moment.

The entire experience has been unprofessional, poorly managed, and wholly unacceptable. What should have been a straightforward consultation became a series of administrative errors, broken commitments, contradictory messages, and avoidable inconvenience. As a prospective patient, I would expect a clinic offering medical and cosmetic treatments to demonstrate significantly higher standards of organisation, communication, and clinical decision-making than those I have experienced throughout this process.

I would not recommend this taxi company- specifically cable taxis at Humberside airport to anyone. If I could give zero stars I would.

This vile woman (owner) and two of her drivers literally went out of their way to prevent a private hire taxi I had pre-booked from taking my children and I home yesterday, leaving us stranded at the airport with no means of getting home.

Uk legislation states that if no car seat is available a child can be transport without one in a taxi, private hire vehicle or public transportation.

I had pre-booked a private hire vehicle from a separate company. We were walking out of the airport with the driver who had come in to kindly assist with our luggage when suddenly we were approached by two taxi drivers from this cable taxi company. They told my driver he could not take us home unless we had car seats for the children (one 7yo and 2yo twins) because it was a private hire and not a taxi. The driver initially believed them and unfortunately left us stranded at the airport despite me telling him that this was not true and we could travel without car seats if one was not available. Uber and Veezu don’t operate here so there was no other option for transport except cable taxis located in Humberside airport- the same ones who, through false information, scared my pre-booked private hire away. Realising I was now stranded with my children, I approached them and asked if they could take us home. The female owner and her two male taxi drivers refused. When I asked why, she said because it is was a “planned journey” we need car seats so she couldn’t take us. I still don’t understand what she meant by planned journey. Planned with whom because I never pre-booked with them. When I mentioned that uk legislation allows children to travel in public transportation without car seats if one is not available, she responded that it’s her company and she determines the rules- not the government or the uk legislation. She spoke to me in the most disrespectful and condescending manner.

I really don’t care whatever she chooses to do with her company and whether she wants to follow the UK legislation or not. But I never chose to hire a taxi with her and I was stranded with my young children because she and her two taxi drivers had approached the private hire I pre-booked from different taxi company and told him not to take us home!!! Then she began to gaslight me saying it was my fault and I should have planned my journey better by taking car seats. Unbelievable.

This cruel woman was actively trying to make my children and I stranded at small rural airport on a Sunday when all the shops were closed, we were in the middle of nowhere and there was virtually no other way to get home- and for a reason I cannot fathom. It’s either she hates children or she is racist because we’re black and honestly having someone act cruelly to us and/or recruiting others to be cruel to us, is sadly not an unfamiliar experience.

Thankfully, our initial pre-booked private hire driver returned after he had also found out that the information given to him by this cable taxi company was false and that he could still take us if no car seats were available. Had he not returned, I would have been completely stranded with young children at the airport, after a long and stressful flight, and with no means of getting home because of the cruel owner of this cable taxi company. I would not recommend them to anyone.

one_star_reviews.text:
Really Disappointed with Take Payments

I normally don’t leave bad reviews, but unfortunately I feel like I have to share my experience with Take Payments because it has been extremely frustrating.

When we signed up, we were told the terminal would cost £1, so naturally that’s what we expected. Instead, we were charged £30 a month for the terminal. That was a huge shock and not what we believed we had agreed to.

On top of that, the terminal itself hasn’t worked properly. The 4G doesn’t work, and the machine won’t connect to our Wi-Fi, which makes it very difficult to actually use the terminal when we need it.

What has really disappointed me is the cancellation process. We tried to cancel after having the machine for only 10 days, but we were told we couldn’t. There was no reasonable cooling-off period or early termination option that would allow us to get out of the agreement.

It honestly feels like we are being forced to keep a machine that we don’t want, while continuing to pay for it even though we’re not able to use it properly.

I understand that businesses have terms and conditions, but there should also be some fairness and understanding when a customer is unhappy with the service after only 10 days, especially when the equipment isn’t even working properly.

Very disappointed with the whole experience. I would think very carefully before signing up with Take Payments.

I was a patient at Aspen Clinic, and I am absolutely furious about the way my friend was let down.
My friend sadly died at General Hospital, but she was under the care and responsibility of Aspen Clinic. She asked for help. She needed help. She was clearly struggling, and yet the support she so desperately needed was not there when it mattered most.
This is not something that should simply be accepted as “one of those things”. A vulnerable person was placed under the care of mental health professionals because she needed to be kept safe. Her pleas for support should have mattered. Her safety should have mattered.
She should still be here.
I sincerely hope there is a full and thorough inquest into what happened. I hope the decisions made, the care provided, the opportunities to intervene and the actions of those responsible for her care are all properly scrutinised. I hope difficult questions are asked, and I hope those responsible are held accountable if the evidence shows that she was failed.
Because this is bigger than a review. A person died. A family lost someone they love. Friends lost someone they cared about. And people deserve answers.
Mental health services have a duty of care. Keeping someone safe cannot just be a responsibility on paper.
I will never forget what happened to my friend, and I sincerely hope her death leads to serious questions, genuine accountability and changes that prevent another person from being failed in the same way.
My thoughts are with her loved ones.

one_star_reviews.text: I spent time in this hell hole as a teenager. Among the huge team of staff, only 3 of them were kind and actually had any desire to help. The rest of them… I have no words to accurately describe the sinister culture of the staff. They would constantly degrade us, pin us against each other and do anything they could to make the horrible time we were having even worse. Sadly, people who dedicate their lives to having unlimited access to vulnerable people often don’t have good intentions… which was perfectly demonstrated here. Just to give a small example of the psychological abuse… I remember on my birthday I was only allowed to have one gift from my family… I got a bottle of perfume that was then kept locked in a small room in the hallway with the rest of our hygiene items… because we were only allowed to have a certain amount in our room at any given time (and that amount frequently changed without warning, depending on the mood of the staff) … one day I came to get a spray of my perfume & noticed half the bottle was empty… I was shocked and I was asking why this happened and a staff member said “oh, I’ve been using it and I’ve been giving sprays to all the other the girls too” with a smug look on her face… I told her that was my special birthday perfume… she laughed in my face and said “well sharing is caring, what are you gonna do about it? Kick off? I dare you” … and this particular staff member was constantly trying to bait us into kicking off so we’d get our levels dropped and she’d get a bonus for restraining us… I didn’t kick off, I was the bigger person and walked away to go cry in the corner and write in my journal. Imagine… a mentally ill 15 year old needing to be the bigger person so I could survive against a bully in their late 40’s. This wasn’t even close to the worse thing that happened to me there. A lot worse things happened and I witnessed a lot worse things happening to others. Like a tiny anorexic girl being restrained by 6 large men, having her clothes cut off her by them, in the middle of the ward…. And god forbid you raise your voice or they’ll inject you with a sedative to completely knock you out. This place is just like the depictions of insane asylums you see in scary movies or read about in history books… I’m begging people to stop sending their children here! Everyone goes in there with one or a couple of issues then develops countless more from the trauma they experience here. Years later and I still struggle with complex PTSD from the things I went through and saw here. I heard this place is getting shut down… I pray that it’s true!

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, after being a client of Jaccountancy for approximately five years, my experience with the firm has ended extremely negatively.

Throughout the relationship there were occasions where deadlines were missed, which caused frustration and concern. I also found the tone and manner of some communications, particularly towards the end of the relationship, unnecessarily rude, dismissive and unprofessional. In my view, this is not how a long-standing client should be spoken to when raising genuine concerns about their account and contractual arrangements.

The situation deteriorated significantly around the latest renewal.

I was sent new engagement documentation which included a substantial increase in my monthly fee. I did not sign the new agreement or expressly agree to the increased fee.

When I subsequently asked to end the relationship, I was informed that the agreement had automatically renewed for another 12 months and that I was liable for an early termination charge based on the remaining fees for that period.

I disputed this, including whether I had agreed to the new renewal terms and increased monthly charge, and raised concerns through the firm’s complaints process.

What followed was, in my experience, extremely disappointing. Despite attempts to resolve the matter, Jaccountancy commenced County Court proceedings against me personally. The claim is disputed and I am defending it.

Something else I subsequently became aware of, which prospective clients may wish to consider when carrying out their own due diligence, is a publicly available disciplinary decision published by the Association of Accounting Technicians (AAT) on 12 May 2026 concerning Jay Wilson, trading as Jaccountancy (UK) Limited and Then Tax Refunds Limited.

The published AAT decision records a finding of misconduct and details a number of matters, including failures concerning anti-money laundering procedures and client due diligence, receiving and retaining commissions without notifying and obtaining consent from relevant clients, client-money compliance issues, and an incorrect licence renewal application submitted to AAT.

According to the published AAT decision, the resulting order included a three-year reprimand, a £6,500 fine and three years ineligibility to apply for fellow membership.

For clarity, the AAT disciplinary decision relates to separate matters and is not a finding concerning my own contractual dispute. I would encourage anyone interested to read the published AAT decision themselves rather than simply relying on my summary.

After approximately five years as a client, I am extremely disappointed that the professional relationship has ended this way.

My advice to anyone considering using Jaccountancy would be to carry out their own due diligence and read every part of the engagement documentation extremely carefully, particularly anything relating to automatic renewal, notice periods, fee increases, early termination charges and personal guarantees. I would also recommend keeping copies of all correspondence and monitoring important filing and submission deadlines yourself.

Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend Jaccountancy.

one_star_reviews.text: I feel it's important to share our experience with ABC 123 The Nannery Ltd. My childrens attended this nursery for over a year and a half with no problems or issues, then all of a sudden the manager, Maria, started what felt like bullying towards us. After choosing not to pay an optional "disbursement" fee, we found ourselves treated very differently to other parents — including being threatened with immediate notice over parking that the manager had previously confirmed in writing was fine. We believe this was discrimination against us as parents simply for not paying the disbursement fee, despite the nursery claiming government funding that is meant to cover children's care costs. We're honestly not sure if it was an ego thing or something else entirely. When we raised concerns about this unfair treatment, we were met with contradictory answers, dismissive responses, and were even accused of "gaslighting" for speaking up. We also received daily update texts about our children's day which showed they had been given a ham sandwich for lunch — despite our children's dietary requirements clearly being on file and this not being met. To top it off, when we tried to leave we were told we now owe £650. Maria owner/manager has also refused to raise this as a formal complaint and has ignored our request for it to be treated as one, which really shows the lack of professionalism here. The staff themselves are lovely and clearly care about the children, but the owner/manager Maria seems to like showing her authority, and that's really let the whole experience down. Trust is everything when it comes to your children's care, and after everything we experienced, we no longer felt that trust was there. We've since given notice, raised a formal complaint with Ofsted, and are sharing this so other parents can make informed choices

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely poor communication and lack of support

I have been extremely disappointed with the way my daughter’s Universal Credit claim has been handled by Consett Jobcentre.

There has been a complete lack of communication between staff, with different people responding to journal messages without apparently having any understanding of the circumstances or what has already been discussed and agreed.

I am my daughter’s appointee and contacted the Jobcentre to have this formally recorded on their system. I was told that a visiting officer would need to be arranged and was asked to provide my full details. I provided everything requested, yet over two weeks later I am still having to chase this and establish whether anything has actually been done.

In the meantime, my daughter has been given appointments at times when I cannot attend because of my work commitments, despite her needing my support. She has then received warnings about potentially being sanctioned for failing to attend.

What makes this particularly frustrating is that her usual member of staff has previously arranged morning appointments so that I can support her. It seems to be the lack of communication between different staff members that is causing the problems.

My daughter is already unwell and signed off sick, yet instead of feeling supported, the constant confusion, repeated explanations and threats of sanctions are causing her considerable additional stress.

I completely understand that staff have to deal with busy workloads, but there needs to be better communication and continuity of care. Vulnerable people should not have to repeatedly explain their circumstances to different members of staff or be put under additional stress because information isn’t being passed between them.

Very disappointing experience and, in my opinion, a service that urgently needs to improve its communication and support.
